before.prompt: If D2 is closely marked before you release, what is sensible?

options.text: Reverse automatically because it was the original plan
Pass through D2’s marker without checking
Reassess a hold or another outlet

before.explanation: A closed second option means another read is needed; holding may be useful if possession can be protected.

after.prompt: YOU want to advance as far toward centre ice as these outlets allow, without sending the puck farther toward the side boards. Which pass would you assess?
after.explanation: C gives more progress toward centre ice than D2 while receiving nearer the middle than the puck is now. W offers more forward distance but is wider. Check the passing line before release: this identifies an option to assess, not a guaranteed safe pass. A reverse to D2 or a wider pass to W may suit a different aim or a changed picture.

optionReasons.reason: W advances 12 m from rendered puck x=-24 but widens |y|6.7 to9; plausible forward width outlet, fails no-wider condition.
C advances 9 m from rendered puck and reduces |y|6.7 to2; more advance than D2 without widening.
D2 x=-24 gives zero advance from rendered puck, with |y|6.7 to6. A reverse is plausible but less advance than C.

limitations: Advisory author; not reviewed, approved or applied.

geometry.units: metres; source x/y; angle in degrees
geometry.method: makeScene canonical owner-facing puck offset; Euclidean point-to-segment distances. One-metre trial positions are analysis examples only, not movement simulation or scored targets.
geometry.limits: Point clearance is not stick/body reach or interception feasibility; endpoint does not prove route safety.

imageDependency: Options require locating named players or rink landmarks relative to YOU; prompt does not supply those positions. Briefing supplies some context, so no claim that image is sole information source.
